name: Theories of evolution, speciation, fossils and resistant bacteria

terms.definition: The remains of organisms from millions of years ago, found in rocks: hard parts that do not decay, mineral replacement, or preserved traces.
terms.examiner: The record is incomplete because many early forms were soft-bodied and geological activity destroyed some fossils.

terms.definition: When there are no remaining individuals of a species still alive.
terms.examiner: Causes include new predators, new diseases, competition and environmental change.

terms.definition: Bacteria with a mutation that survives antibiotic treatment, so resistant bacteria reproduce and spread, as with MRSA.
terms.examiner: To reduce it: don't prescribe for viral infections, complete the course, restrict use in farming.

terms.definition: Proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection, published in On the Origin of Species (1859).
terms.examiner: Separate Biology. Initially controversial: little evidence at the time, and it challenged the idea of creation.

terms.definition: Proposed that changes acquired during an organism's life are inherited; now rejected.
The formation of a new species when populations become isolated and their characteristics change until they can no longer interbreed.
terms.examiner: Separate Biology. Wallace worked on speciation and warning colouration.
